bm.flows method names are the flow name camelCased. The flow NAME comes from: (a) a single-job file under flows/ → the FILE stem (flows/company-setup.yaml → flow `company-setup` → bm.flows.companySetup), (b) root flows.yaml or a multi-job file → each JOB key (jobs: {send_invite: …} → bm.flows.sendInvite). A request trigger takes one job per file: several jobs there would share its route and are refused when written.

A kebab-named flow is keyed by its camelCase name in /_internal/flows.json and the generated FlowMap (flows/save-quote.yaml → bm.flows.saveQuote). bm.flows['save-quote'] also works and is typed as an alias, and FlowForm({flow}) accepts the same spellings. When two flow names camelCase alike (save-quote and save_quote), the one already spelled as the key keeps it, else the first by name, and the other keeps its own name.

snake_case / kebab-case spellings also resolve (bm.flows.company_setup works), and a wrong name throws an error that LISTS every flow the caller may call. The registry is GET /_internal/flows.json and it is PER CALLER: anonymous visitors see only flows without `auth: required`/`role:`, signed-in users add auth-required flows, role holders add their role's flows, admins see everything. Signature-verified webhook flows (`verify:`) are listed for admins only. The SDK refetches the registry once on a miss, so signing in mid-session works.
Escape hatch that always works: bm.api.post('/api/company-setup', body) - the flow's HTTP path doesn't depend on the SDK mapping.
